methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free community AI workshops by a local native directly targets broad capability building in a non-metro region, signaling grassroots distributed learning that could counter concentration dynamics if scaled beyond initial cohorts.

signals.title: TAYLOR: AI data centers increase Virginia’s urban-rural divide - The Cavalier Daily
signals.signal_reading: Data center concentration in NoVA explicitly widens urban-rural divide through infrastructure investment patterns that extract value from rural land without building local technical capacity or distributed AI capability.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU-AI Ready RVA partnership deepens metro Richmond's AI ecosystem through formal institutional coordination, but concentration in the capital region reinforces hub-spoke patterns rather than distributed capability.

signals.title: University of Mary Washington Adds Virginia’s First Master’s Degree in AI in Business - Northern Virginia Magazine
signals.signal_reading: Virginia's first AI business master's degree at UMW creates specialized credentialing infrastructure, but graduate-level programs concentrate depth among already-credentialed populations rather than distributing foundational AI literacy broadly.

signals.title: Tony Stark’s J.A.R.V.I.S., Meet Amelia, Norfolk Naval Shipyard’s IT AI Help Assistant - DVIDS
signals.signal_reading: Norfolk Naval Shipyard's AI help assistant 'Amelia' represents platform-delivered shallow adoption—efficiency gains through conversational interfaces that don't require workforce AI fluency or capability to build/customize systems.
